checks.why: a method whose only outgoing calls are ambient used to answer '0 methods reached' and stop — a dead end, although the graph holds the word written at both call sites. Java and Python name their boundary (boundary_lib); JavaScript and TypeScript record no callee at all on theirs (ambient_terminal), so it was never listed (#1107)

and it is NOT called 'calls into libraries': an ambient_terminal edge means the callee is ambient or the receiver is untyped, which on this language is as often a method of the project as a platform one, so calling it a library would assert a resolution that was never made
a resolved chain is unaffected: the two client calls still connect and still carry their kind and call site
